question: True or false: NBA players shoot free throws noticeably worse in the final seconds of very close games?
answer: True. Cao, Price and Stone studied eight NBA seasons of free throws: in the dying seconds of very close games, players shot 5 to 10 percentage points below their usual rate. The drop was biggest for weaker shooters and on a second attempt after missing the first. The basket does not move; the stakes do.
move: Practise a routine under the conditions in which it will count.
ask: Where do I practise only when nothing is at stake, then expect the same result under pressure?
trap: Assuming professionals are immune to pressure on a routine shot.
source: Cao, Price & Stone, J Sports Econ, 2011
reference: Zheng Cao, Joseph Price & Daniel F. Stone, Performance Under Pressure in the NBA, Journal of Sports Economics, 2011
